subject.title: [Feature] Re-enable dev channel distribution tag for npm releases

question: Should OpenClaw permanently treat moving-main `dev` as git-only, or support a second npm experimental channel alongside Tideclaw `alpha`?
rationale: The code can support either direction, but channel identity, publication cadence, versioning, provenance, and credential exposure are release-policy choices that automation cannot safely infer.

options.title: Make dev git-only
options.body: Document `dev` as the moving `main` git path and remove npm `dev` references, leaving `alpha` as the only gated npm experimental track.

options.title: Publish npm dev snapshots
options.body: Define unique snapshot versions and add a gated moving-main workflow with provenance, cancellation, tests, and registry verification under npm `dev`.

options.title: Alias dev to alpha
options.body: Mirror selected Tideclaw alpha versions onto npm `dev` only after explicitly documenting that `dev` is not literal moving-main head.

recommendation.title: Make dev git-only
recommendation.body: Document `dev` as the moving `main` git path and remove npm `dev` references, leaving `alpha` as the only gated npm experimental track.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history and the existing issue analysis connect this person to the affected release workflow, helpers, and channel documentation.
